text:
incidents-bot: 🔔 Paging: p99 latency spike detected for hosted-api /v1/generate in eu-west-1 — p99 ~ 4.2s (SLO breach). Alert level: high. Affected routes: /v1/generate (streaming), /v1/chat/completions (some).
Emma (SRE): acked. joining. any customer impact yet?
Raj (Runtime): seeing elevated tail on streaming workers, p95 ~1.1s -> p99 4s+. KV cache hit rate dropped ~40% in last 3m.
Oncall-Ops: I'm oncall. grabbing dashboards now — posting links.
Raj (Runtime): dash: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streams/latency?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west-1 (paste)
Emma (SRE): loading. looks correlated with recent worker pool restart at ~1898765400. Could be rolling restart noise or kvcache warmup.
Maria (Customer Success): any customers seeing errors or rate limits? CS noticing increased tickets for slow responses on chat features. No 5xxs so far.
Emma (SRE): quick checks: 1) is autoscaler chopping pods? 2) any OOMs on runtime? 3) KV cache eviction rate?
Raj (Runtime): autoscaler stable, no scale events in last 10m. small number of reconnects to cache nodes, eviction spikes on node eu-cache-2.
Oncall-Ops: running quick k/v health check: `curl -sS http://eu-cache-2.internal/health | jq .` -> `{\"status\":\"degraded\",\"evictions\":732}`
Emma (SRE): ok that explains hit rate drop. mitigation options: a) route streaming to dedicated pool in eu-west-1, b) temporarily increase cache replica for eu, c) failover to fallback model variant w/ smaller context for streaming (less KV pressure).
Raj (Runtime): I can flip routing to dedicated for streaming routes; that'll add cost but reduce tail. prepping a traffic-shift runbook step.
Oncall-Ops: doing lightweight mitigation: enabling route override to dedicated pool (2m expected).
incidents-bot: ACTION: runbook step invoked by Oncall-Ops — "Shift streaming -> dedicated-eu".
Emma (SRE): also notifying infra team to restart eu-cache-2 gracefully (non-disruptive drain). Raj, can you put a temporary TTL increase to reduce eviction pressure?
Raj (Runtime): applying `cache.eviction_policy.set(\"ttl_seconds\", 900)` to eu-cache-2 via infra API.
Raj (Runtime): applied. monitoring.
Maria (Customer Success): I'll post a short status note to affected customers: "We've detected elevated latency in EU for streaming; our oncall team is actively mitigating and expect improvements in the next 10 minutes." Want me to send?
Emma (SRE): yes, please. include that no data was lost and we're doing a routing/replica change.
Maria (Customer Success): sent to impacted list.
incidents-bot: METRIC: p99 for /v1/generate eu-west-1: 4.2s -> 3.0s (2m after mitigation).
Oncall-Ops: new p99 trending 2.9s, p95 back to ~0.9s. still above SLO but improving. keep monitoring 10m window.
Raj (Runtime): cache evictions dropping, connections to eu-cache-2 re-established. suspected root: degraded cache node after kernel patch earlier today. raising infra ticket.
Emma (SRE): good. I'll keep the routing override for 30m and then gradually revert once p99 < 1.5s for 10m. Can someone own postmortem? needs timeline + why cache wasn't auto-drained earlier.
Raj (Runtime): I'll own postmortem. will gather logs, eviction history, worker-restart timeline.
Oncall-Ops: handing off to Raj for postmortem. I'm available if we need further mitigations. Closing oncall handoff in this thread.
sre-runbook-bot: Reminder: create incident ticket in JIRA using template `INC-LATENCY-STREAMING` and link this thread.
Raj (Runtime): created INC-2026-3245, attached logs.
Emma (SRE): thanks. final status: mitigation applied (routing + cache TTL), customer notifications sent, infra ticket opened. will drop a follow-up with postmortem when ready. :thumbsup:
Maria (Customer Success): thx everyone — customers acknowledged update.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated): p99 trending down; closing paging but keep incident open for postmortem actions.
